speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me identify the cause, can you tell me if this spinning sensation happens constantly or comes in brief, discrete episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Given the sudden onset lasting only 3 minutes while in a supine position, followed by a return to baseline, this strongly suggests BPPV. Have you noticed that turning your head in bed or looking up triggers similar brief episodes?
